neighbours.label: epistemic 'could'/'may' that offers a possible interpretation or outcome, as against 'could' of past ability, 'may' of permission, and plain assertions
fire: The scratches on the bone could indicate that early humans used tools.
Historians think the letter could have been written by his sister.
A sudden drop in prices could easily push smaller farms into debt.
Some of these stars may be much older than the galaxy itself.
The strange symbol on the map could mark an old well.
The new findings may be evidence of water beneath the ice.
Experts warn that the virus could spread quickly in crowded cities.
The missing page could explain why the plan was abandoned.
quiet: As a boy he could run faster than anyone in his school.
Historians know the letter was written by his sister.
Visitors may park in the lot behind the museum.
Some of these stars are much older than the galaxy itself.
The strange symbol on the map marks an old well.
Students may borrow up to five books at a time.
Before the accident she could play the piano for hours.
The missing page explains why the plan was abandoned.
